instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Consensus Means Me
cards.instruction: Treat every partial agreement as confirmation that everyone has accepted your leadership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I nodded when you nodded. Friday it is; I'll tell the committee they've accepted me as project lead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I nodded because Friday suits me. We weren't voting for a leader.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, scheduling first. Everyone's happy to follow my timetable, then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll attend, but I'll vote against your budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, you'll be my finance watchdog. I'll put you first on the agenda for my meeting.

beats.text: I've given the volunteers a thumbs-up like you. They're happy with me leading the campaign, then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant I could read the blue poster from here. We still need to choose a slogan together.

beats.speaker: B

beats.text: Perfect. I'll tell them their first job under me is choosing the slogan.

cards.title: Expand Your Jurisdiction
cards.instruction: Use every new problem as a reason to expand what you are entitled to control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I copied your red tag onto my key. I need it to control the kitchen; Accounts keeps missing tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Red marks a spare, not a master key. It'll open the kitchen, but the cleaners lock the kettle in their cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the spare. Give me approval of their checklist as well, so the kettle stays out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Their contractor only takes instructions from the building manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then send the manager's instructions through me. I can't keep Accounts supplied if someone else can order the kettle away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've circled the roads on your delivery map too. All those routes will need my approval before vans arrive during meetings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My circles mark roadworks. You book the rooms, not the roads. I'll send you our arrival times.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the blocked routes. Send me your alternatives and I'll choose ones that fit the meeting schedule.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The council changes the closures overnight. Even we can't choose a reliable route.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give the council my booking calendar. They can clear their changes with me before they put the barriers out.

cards.title: Be There for Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to show up, help, or stay involved as proof that the connection still matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Save me the seat beside you at pottery. I've taken my shoes off like yours; we hardly do anything together now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine are drying by the heater. I'm only dropping you off; clay hurts my fingers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, drying first. Sit beside me anyway. You can choose the glaze and I'll do the clay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not making anything. I can stay and have a cup of tea, that's all.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll have tea too. I'd rather sit beside you than take another pot home on my own.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dad, I've put a red dot on your invitation like you did on that sculpture label. Your place at my opening is reserved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The dot means sold. I was marking a sale for you, not booking a seat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the sales dot. Keep the invitation; I still want you beside me when people come in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your mother will be there. We haven't spoken since the divorce.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come before we open. Help me unpack the biggest piece; I want a bit of tonight with you in it too.

cards.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've washed my cup after yours. There, a fresh start. Stay a bit longer; I don't want you leaving while we're still angry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I rinsed mine because the tea was cold. I stayed to clean up, and that's done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. The kitchen's finished. Could you stay until we can talk without snapping?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got ten minutes before the last bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me nine, then. Leave the cups where they are and tell me what you're still angry about.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There, my phone's face down like yours. We're making peace. Don't call the taxi until we've settled last night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I turned mine over because the screen kept lighting up. I've apologized for telling my sister about your debt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Leave it down for a minute; I can't face her watching what I order at dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's already paid for the meal. We'll be late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sit with me before we go. I need to know you'll be there as my partner, not to tell her how grateful I was.

cards.title: Name What It Cost
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the emotional cost of what happened, not merely the event itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've sent a thumbs-up like yours. Apology accepted. Now tell me you understand why six weeks without an answer hurt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine only meant I'd received your message. My phone was broken; I wasn't sending an apology.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, received. I didn't get a repair notice, though. What did those six weeks look like from my end?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You thought I'd stopped caring. I can see why you'd stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I didn't stop. I kept rewriting the same message to make it easier to answer. Can you understand what that did to me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've copied your smile for our happy concert memory. Now tell me you understand what your empty seat felt like.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I smiled because you played the encore beautifully. My train was cancelled; I wanted to be there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Watch my face before the encore. Can you see what waiting for you was doing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saw you look at the door just before you started. You thought I might still come.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Say you understand that I was still saving part of the evening for you, even while I was playing.
